notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware or sim run was made. panda-gym was not importable where the gate ran (it needs gymnasium, pybullet, numpy<2 and scipy, setup.py:23), so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python stand-in for PandaReach-v3 (fake.py) and was not compared with a PyBullet run; the sim backend (gymnasium.make('PandaReach-v3')) was not run. The fake draws goals with Python's random.Random instead of numpy's generator, moves the end-effector directly instead of through inverse kinematics and 20 physics substeps, applies the 50-step TimeLimit that gymnasium.make adds, and starts from a placeholder end-effector position; all of this is in the fidelity gaps. The real observation sizes (6 robot position/velocity values, 3 achieved-goal and 3 desired-goal values) match the fake, so no array is reduced. NOT COVERED: rendering (render_mode human/rgb_array is not served) and the PyBullet physics itself. Five warnings are expected of this Gymnasium family driver: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs (seed twice, ticks and action.values); declaring actions was not used because it exposes the reset scenario/options without descriptions, as the Gymnasium exemplar documents. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the check report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
